claim_text: An agent is a model plus a harness, where the harness is the scaffolding around the model that connects it to the real world.
evidence_span: The harness is the scaffolding around the model that connects it to the real world.

claim_text: An agent is only as good as the context provided to the model, so the job of a harness is to provide that context at every step.
evidence_span: 1. An agent is only as good as the context provided to the model 2. The job of a harness is to provide context to the model at every step

claim_text: LangChain's create_agent is purposefully minimalistic: it implements only the core agent loop and exposes middleware as the primitive for customization.
evidence_span: `create_agent` just implements the core agent loop, and it exposes **middleware** as a primitive for customization.

claim_text: Middleware hooks into the agent loop before and after model calls, before and after tool calls, and at agent startup and teardown, with each piece handling one concern and composing freely with any other.
evidence_span: Middleware hooks into the agent loop at each step: before and after model calls, before and after tool calls, at agent startup and teardown. Each piece handles one concern and composes freely with any other

claim_text: Deterministic middleware logic is the right place for anything that cannot or should not live in a prompt: business logic, policy enforcement, swapping the model by task complexity, adjusting the prompt, and updating message history during compaction.
evidence_span: **Deterministic Logic.** Business logic, policy enforcement, dynamic agent control — anything that needs to fire at a specific point in the loop. This includes runtime control over the agent itself: swapping the model based on task complexity, adjusting the prompt, and updating the agent's message history (during compaction, for example). The right place for anything that can't (or shouldn't) live in a prompt.

claim_text: Because each middleware piece is isolated, the same middleware can be reused across every agent in an organization so new agents inherit battle-tested behavior without rebuilding it.
evidence_span: Because each piece is isolated, the same middleware can be reused across every agent in an organization so that new agents inherit battle-tested behavior without rebuilding it.

claim_text: Pre-assembled harnesses such as Deep Agents and the Claude Agent SDK reach a production-ready agent fast and work for most cases, but many agents need finer-grained customization than they support, including custom prompting, business logic, and guardrails.
evidence_span: They're designed to get you to a production-ready agent fast, and they work well for most cases. But many agents need finer grained customization than these harnesses support: custom prompting, business logic, guardrails, etc.

claim_text: Long-running sessions accumulate message history fast and overflow the context window without intervention, which summarization and context-editing middleware exist to prevent.
evidence_span: | Prevent context overflow | Long-running sessions accumulate message history fast. Without intervention, it overflows the context window. | SummarizationMiddleware, ContextEditingMiddleware |

claim_text: Subagents handle complex sub-tasks with clean context windows while a todo list tracks progress across a long run.
evidence_span: | Delegate tasks | Subagents handle complex sub-tasks with clean context windows. A todo list tracks progress across a long run. | SubAgentMiddleware, AsyncSubAgentMiddleware, TodoListMiddleware |

claim_text: Policy enforcement such as PII handling, compliance checks, and approval gates must fire on every call regardless of what the model does, so it does not belong in a prompt.
evidence_span: | Enforce policies | PII handling, compliance checks, approval gates — these need to fire on every call regardless of what the model does. They don't belong in a prompt. | PIIMiddleware, HumanInTheLoopMiddleware |

claim_text: Task-harness fit is how well a harness matches the actual demands of the task, meaning the context it needs, the failures it will encounter, the policies it must enforce, and the environment it operates in.
evidence_span: Task-harness fit is how well your harness matches the actual demands of the task: the context it needs, the failures it'll encounter, the policies it must enforce, the environment it operates in. A harness for a customer service agent looks very different from one built for a long-running coding agent.

claim_text: How well a harness fits the task at hand determines how useful an agent is.
evidence_span: How well a harness fits the task at hand determines how useful an agent is.
